title: Hide a name or an email in a screenshot before you hand it over
goal: A redline goes out with a real screen in it: somebody’s name, their email, an account number, a customer logo. Photonz has no way to cover any of it. You can blur a shape you drew, which blurs the shape, not the picture under it. Everyone who shares screenshots hides something in them first, and today that means finishing the job somewhere else.
notes:
BLOCKED on its decision card until the user answers: this adds a visible tool nobody asked for, and the manager rule after the 2026-09-02 capture loupe is that competitor-parity controls get a card first.

Why it is a small piece of work despite being a new tool. The renderer already composites a layer against the picture beneath it: Sources/PhotonzRender/DocumentRenderer.swift line 647, "backdrop is the composite of all visible layers below this one", which is how a zoom callout magnifies live rather than baking a copy. A cover reads the same backdrop and blurs or pixelates it instead of magnifying it, so it is the zoom callout seam with a different filter.

What exists today, checked on 2026-09-09: EffectKind in Sources/PhotonzCore/LayerEffects.swift is blur, shadow, border, glow, and blur is applied to the layer’s own image (DocumentRenderer.swift:856). Nothing in Sources matches pixelate, redact or spotlight. Sources/PhotonzCore/Tools.swift has no cover tool.

The export question in the acceptance matters more than it looks: a blur that is only a view-time effect can be undone by anyone who gets the document, which for this feature is the whole point of it.

CleanShot X ships this as two things, secure blur and pixelate, and it is one of the features its reviews lead with (docs/plan/competitive-cleanshot.md).
acceptance: Drag out a box over part of a capture and what is under it stops being readable, without changing the picture underneath, so it can be moved, resized and undone like any other layer
Ships behind its own flag in Next, off by default until it is tried; the flag name goes in the audit
It survives an export and a copy to the clipboard: what leaves the app is covered, and the original pixels are not recoverable from the exported file
To see it: Scripts/probe-app.sh with a screenshot open, pick the tool, drag a box over some words, then move the box and watch it keep covering
anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task

log.note: Adds a visible tool nobody asked for, so it waits on its decision card.
